citation: Murphy, R., Weinhardt, F., & Wyness, G. (2021). Who teaches the teachers? A RCT of peer-to-peer observation and feedback in 181 schools. Economics of Education Review, 82, 102091. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.econedurev.2021.102091
report_number: Economics of Education Review 82 (2021) 102091; DOI 10.1016/j.econedurev.2021.102091. Numbers extracted from the legal open pre-publication version: CEP Discussion Paper No. 1565 (August 2018), LSE Centre for Economic Performance (= IZA DP 11731 = DIW DP 1753, identical draft). AEA RCT registry trial #1779. Evaluation also published as the EEF 'Lesson Study' project report.
url: https://cep.lse.ac.uk/pubs/download/dp1565.pdf (LSE CEP institutional repository; identical copy also at https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED593175.pdf [ERIC] and https://docs.iza.org/dp11731.pdf [IZA])
design: Cluster RCT, randomised at SCHOOL level (pairwise stratified randomisation by Local Authority). 181 eligible state primary schools in England (89 allocated treatment / 92 control; 167 in the matched-pair analysis sample). 543 teachers, ~13,000 pupils across two cohorts (cohort 1 N=6,436; cohort 2 N=6,298). Intervention = teacher peer-to-peer lesson observation and feedback (Lesson Study/'learning tripod' of three Year 4-5 teachers; 18 lesson observations over 2 years; five full training days delivered by external educational experts at Edge Hill University). Two-year programme, concentrated in year 1; cohort 1 exposed to 1 year, cohort 2 to the full 2 years. Comparison = business-as-usual (control schools received no treatment, training, or materials). Outcomes = national, compulsory, externally-marked KS2 (age-11) tests taken ONE YEAR after the intervention ended: combined maths+reading 'Test Score' (pre-specified primary), maths, reading, SPAG (spelling/punctuation/grammar), and science (teacher-assessed, cohort 1 only). ITT pupil-level OLS with pair fixed effects, age-7 (KS1) baseline test scores, and pupil demographics; SEs clustered at school level. Grade band 3-6 (intervention in Years 4-5 = US grades 3-4; tested at end of Year 6 = grade 5-6). Meta-analysis coding (row 82): School/RCT/Published, grades 3-6, Average/High SES, goal '(P)CK', External trainer, Long duration.
problems: VERSION PROVENANCE: the meta-analysis cites the published Economics of Education Review 2021 article (DOI 10.1016/j.econedurev.2021.102091), which is PAYWALLED (Unpaywall/OpenAlex: closed, no OA copy). Per spec I used the legal open pre-publication version (CEP Discussion Paper No. 1565, Aug 2018 = IZA DP 11731 = DIW DP 1753, the SAME pre-registered RCT and statistical analysis plan). The 2018 working-paper abstract states it can 'reject positive effects of about ten percent of a standard deviation across all subjects, and effect sizes larger than five percent of a standard deviation in reading and writing tests' - consistent with the paper's null finding. Numbers in the final published EER version may differ marginally from this draft; if central records need the published values, institutional access to the EER article is required to confirm. SAMPLE-SIZE SPLIT: the report does NOT publish the treatment/control STUDENT n split for either cohort - only the per-cohort totals (cohort 1 = 6,436; cohort 2 = 6,298). n_t/n_c therefore left null; total per-cohort N recorded in notes and the school allocation (89 treatment / 92 control, 167 matched-pair analysis schools) recorded in n_clusters/notes. ICC not reported (left null); SEs are already clustered at school level so cluster_adjusted=true. EFFECT SIZE SOURCE: g is taken from Table 4 column 5 ('Standardised'), the fully-controlled ITT specification (pair FX + age-7 baseline + demographics) reported directly in SD units by the authors; this is the pretest-adjusted, school-clustered standardised mean difference. Small-sample correction J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = N-2 is ~0.99988 (negligible at N~6,400), so g ~= reported standardised effect and g_se ~= reported standardised SE. TWO COHORTS = two distinct pupil samples with different treatment dose (cohort 1 = 1 year; cohort 2 = full 2-year programme). Both extracted as separate effect sizes per the spec's '(arm x subject x test x sample x timepoint)' rule; cohort 2 is the end-of-full-treatment/full-dose wave. GOAL CODING NOTE: the meta-analysis coded this study's TPD goal as '(P)CK', but the intervention is a peer-observation/feedback (Lesson Study) programme rather than an explicit subject-content-knowledge programme - flagged for the authors. Combined 'Test Score' is a cross-subject composite (maths+reading) recorded with outcome_role=composite; the per-subject maths/reading/SPAG/science rows are the components (outcome_role=secondary, the paper's secondary outcomes; the paper's headline/primary is the combined Test Score). Science was teacher-assessed on a 13-level coarse scale (not percentilised) and available for cohort 1 only.

effect_sizes.timepoint: post (age-11 KS2, 2015/16; one year after end of 2-year intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: g taken directly from Table 4 (p.33/PDF p.35) Panel B (cohort 2), Maths row, column 5 'Standardised' = 0.035 (SE 0.046). This is the fully-controlled ITT standardised mean difference (pair FX + age-7 baseline + demographics, SE clustered at school level). J = 1-3/(4*(6298-2)-1) = 0.99988 (negligible), so g = J*d = 0.035, g_se = J*SE = 0.04599, g_var = g_se^2. mean_t/mean_c are the unconditional treatment/control percentile means from Table 3 Panel B (cross-sectional); SDs of percentile not reported.
